symbolic_guard: shared inherited IO phase plus static ParamRTL port-shape validation
rationale: MorphVerilog runs the inherited IO-shape guard on the concrete witness, while ParamRTL retains a static named port direction and packed-type schema for every legal parameter value.

symbolic_guard: shared inherited hierarchy phase plus ParamRTL module dependency, mixed-local dependency, generate-scope and typed named-binding validation
rationale: MorphVerilog runs the inherited hierarchy phase on the concrete witness; ParamRTL separately validates the symbolic module graph, typed bindings, one combined local graph, bounded generate-for scope, both generate-if branches and every generate-case choice/default, while default-shape recursion substitutes bindings and recomputes mixed locals per instance.

symbolic_guard: ParamRTL symbolic expression, mixed local-parameter, Boolean-expression, integer-comparison, conditional-integer, indexed-part-select and runtime-process type proof
rationale: The concrete witness runs the shared inherited phase and the guarded frontend preserves implemented constant expressions and direct runtime-process port references for ParamRTL proof. Bound public defaults are evaluated per instance before the combined dependency-first local graph, conditional child locals and widths are recomputed. Combinational conditions and sequential clock/reset/enable controls are exact unsigned one-bit inputs, while runtime data paths are exactly type-compatible with their targets for the complete legal width domain. Conditional intervals conservatively hull both branches without guard correlation; general runtime expressions, minimum, maximum and clog2 remain planned.

symbolic_guard: predicate-aware ParamRTL driver and bounded process coverage
rationale: The concrete witness runs the inherited phase and ParamRTL proves exact output coverage for canonical generate-for, generate-if and generate-case configurations, both paths of one complete CombinationalIf, and sole ownership by each atomic register variant. Each enabled register's absent disabled assignment is proven intentional sequential hold, not combinational incompleteness. Mixed procedural/structural drivers fail before emission; general expressions, multiple or nested runtime statements and broader sequential forms keep the guard partial.

symbolic_guard: atomic ParamRTL reset/capture/hold completeness and ownership proof
rationale: Increments 16 through 19 admit atomic rising-edge registers only when the sole output has a complete active-high reset-to-zero path, a complete direct-input capture path and, for either enabled variant, explicit disabled hold semantics with reset priority. No sibling process, hierarchy, generate or continuous driver is allowed. General clocked statements, arbitrary hold values, multiple registers and register coverage across parameterized branches remain unimplemented, so the broader disposition is partial.

symbolic_guard: shared graph check plus symbolic generate analysis
rationale: The Increment 15 direct input-to-output combinational process and Increment 16 through 19 direct input-to-register-output processes cannot encode a combinational feedback edge, while the inherited concrete graph guard still runs. Intentional enabled hold is state feedback, not a combinational path. General runtime expressions require a ParamRTL dependency-graph adaptation before this disposition can advance.

symbolic_guard: one-clock bounded process restriction plus shared concrete CDC check
rationale: Increments 16 through 19 each encode one validated unsigned one-bit input clock and forbid sibling processes, hierarchy and generate structure, so an internal multi-domain crossing is unrepresentable in each tranche. They do not model or approve external input-domain provenance, multiple clocks or CDC structures, so the broader CDC disposition remains partial.
The shared finalizer rejects leaked DSL and clock-domain stacks after configured phase inserters; PhaseContext.doPhase independently keeps every pending phase error fatal.
